newsitem.title: INDONESIA: No special security for festive season in Timor.
newsitem.headline: No special security for festive season in Timor.

text.p: Indonesia's military commander in the former Portuguese colony of East Timor said there was no need for special security arrangements for the Christmas and New Year period, the official Antara news agency reported on Monday.

"Security problems in this region will be dealt with in accordance with existing procedures, so there is no need for special security with regard to Christmas and New Year. It's all the same," said East Timor military chief Colonel Mahidin Simbolon.
Reports have said U.S. Congressman Patrick Kennedy and several foreign diplomats were expected to visit East Timor, which is mostly Roman Catholic, over Christmas.

Antara said that General Feisal Tanjung, head of the armed forces in mostly Moslem Indonesia, was also expected to visit East Timor on December 27 to take part in a government-sponsored Christmas celebration in the capital of Dili.

Indonesia invaded East Timor in December 1975 and declared the territory its 27th province the following July, a move not recognised by the United Nations, which still regards Portugal as the administering power.

The problems of the territory were in the spotlight after Bishop Carlos Belo, the most senior clergyman in East Timor, was awarded the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize jointly with self-exiled East Timor independence advocate Jose Ramos Horta.
